# Personal Income and Outlays, September 2026

[**Personal income** increased $54.5 billion](https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=19&step=2&isuri=1&categories=survey&_gl=1*kvcm30*_ga*MjA4Njg2MTcyMS4xNzQ4MzU1NTcy*_ga_J4698JNNFT*czE3NTQ5MTg5MzIkbzg0JGcxJHQxNzU0OTIyMTUyJGo1NiRsMCRoMA..#eyJhcHBpZCI6MTksInN0ZXBzIjpbMSwyLDNdLCJkYXRhIjpbWyJjYXRlZ29yaWVzIiwiU3VydmV5Il0sWyJOSVBBX1RhYmxlX0xpc3QiLCI3NiJdXX0=) (0.2 percent at a monthly rate) in September, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). **Disposable personal income (DPI)**—personal income less personal current taxes—increased $52.7 billion (0.2 percent), and **personal consumption expenditures (PCE)** increased $113.1 billion (0.5 percent).

[![Disposable Personal Income, Outlays, and Saving](https://www.bea.gov/system/files/pi0926chart1.png)](/system/files/pi0926chart1.png)

**Personal outlays**—the sum of PCE, personal interest payments, and personal current transfer payments—increased $113.0 billion in September. **Personal saving** was $911.1 billion, and the **personal saving rate**—personal saving as a percentage of DPI—was 3.8 percent.

The increase in **current-dollar personal income** in September primarily reflected increases in compensation and government social benefits.

The [$113.1 billion increase in **current-dollar PCE**](https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=19&step=2&isuri=1&categories=survey&_gl=1*kvcm30*_ga*MjA4Njg2MTcyMS4xNzQ4MzU1NTcy*_ga_J4698JNNFT*czE3NTQ5MTg5MzIkbzg0JGcxJHQxNzU0OTIyMTUyJGo1NiRsMCRoMA..#eyJhcHBpZCI6MTksInN0ZXBzIjpbMSwyLDNdLCJkYXRhIjpbWyJjYXRlZ29yaWVzIiwiU3VydmV5Il0sWyJOSVBBX1RhYmxlX0xpc3QiLCI4MiJdXX0=) in September reflected increases of $35.1 billion in spending on goods and $78.1 billion in spending on services.

[![Changes in Monthly Consumer Spending September 2026](https://www.bea.gov/system/files/pi0926chart2.png)](/system/files/pi0926chart2.png)

[**Real PCE** increased $2.6 billion](https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=19&step=2&isuri=1&categories=survey&_gl=1*kvcm30*_ga*MjA4Njg2MTcyMS4xNzQ4MzU1NTcy*_ga_J4698JNNFT*czE3NTQ5MTg5MzIkbzg0JGcxJHQxNzU0OTIyMTUyJGo1NiRsMCRoMA..#eyJhcHBpZCI6MTksInN0ZXBzIjpbMSwyLDNdLCJkYXRhIjpbWyJjYXRlZ29yaWVzIiwiU3VydmV5Il0sWyJOSVBBX1RhYmxlX0xpc3QiLCI4MyJdXX0=) ([less than 0.1 percent](https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=19&step=2&isuri=1&categories=survey&_gl=1*kvcm30*_ga*MjA4Njg2MTcyMS4xNzQ4MzU1NTcy*_ga_J4698JNNFT*czE3NTQ5MTg5MzIkbzg0JGcxJHQxNzU0OTIyMTUyJGo1NiRsMCRoMA..#eyJhcHBpZCI6MTksInN0ZXBzIjpbMSwyLDNdLCJkYXRhIjpbWyJjYXRlZ29yaWVzIiwiU3VydmV5Il0sWyJOSVBBX1RhYmxlX0xpc3QiLCI3OSJdXX0=) at a monthly rate) in September.

[From the preceding month, the **PCE price index** for September increased 0.5 percent](https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=19&step=2&isuri=1&categories=survey&_gl=1*1p5v1ex*_ga*MjA4Njg2MTcyMS4xNzQ4MzU1NTcy*_ga_J4698JNNFT*czE3NTUwOTMyMTUkbzg5JGcxJHQxNzU1MDkzMjE4JGo1NyRsMCRoMA..#eyJhcHBpZCI6MTksInN0ZXBzIjpbMSwyLDNdLCJkYXRhIjpbWyJjYXRlZ29yaWVzIiwiU3VydmV5Il0sWyJOSVBBX1RhYmxlX0xpc3QiLCI4NCJdXX0=). Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index increased 0.3 percent.

[From the same month one year ago, the **PCE price index** for September increased 3.6 percent](https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=19&step=2&isuri=1&categories=survey&_gl=1*1p5v1ex*_ga*MjA4Njg2MTcyMS4xNzQ4MzU1NTcy*_ga_J4698JNNFT*czE3NTUwOTMyMTUkbzg5JGcxJHQxNzU1MDkzMjE4JGo1NyRsMCRoMA..#eyJhcHBpZCI6MTksInN0ZXBzIjpbMSwyLDNdLCJkYXRhIjpbWyJjYXRlZ29yaWVzIiwiU3VydmV5Il0sWyJOSVBBX1RhYmxlX0xpc3QiLCI0MjQiXV19). Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index increased 3.1 percent from one year ago.

## **Technical Notes**

### Changes in personal income and outlays for September

The September increase of $54.5 billion in personal income primarily reflected increases in compensation and government social benefits.

-   Within compensation, the increase was led by private wages and salaries based on U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics’ (BLS) Current Employment Statistics (CES).
-   The increase in government social benefits was led by Medicare, based on data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and the Budget of the U.S. Government.

### Revisions to personal income

Estimates have been updated for July and August reflecting revised BLS CES data. The revision to personal interest income was led by monetary interest, based on newly available data from the U.S. Bureau of the Fiscal Service.
